newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products firm on regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products firm on regional demand.

text.p: Singapore oil products prices remained firm on Wednesday as regional demand for jet fuel and gas oil remained steady, while Chinese fuel oil demand is emerging for December, traders said.

Gas oil rallied to trade at yet another five-year high of $30.80 when a European major sold 150,000 barrels to a Singapore trader for Dec 1-5 lifting fob, 20 cents over the last deal on Friday. The buyer was still seeking cargoes at $30.80. Traders said Indonesia continued its year-end buying spree with its purchase of around three million barrels for December arrival. Indonesia bought nearky six million barrels for November.

Some traders said India might buy larger volumes of gas oil for January, but others said its January imports would hover around or below its December purchases. The swaps market earlier came under pressure from talk that a trader who is taking delivery of 865,000 tonnes of gas oil on the expiry of the IPE November contract might ship 250,000 tonnes to Asia. Taiwan's gas oil sale tender for Dec 11-30 lifting saw bids under $29.95 a barrel fob. Jet fuel is getting support from Japan and S.Korea as winter nears with eight cargoes bought for December/January. A Japanese refiner was heard to have bought two more jet cargoes for December around $1.65 premium c+f but was not confirmed.

Despite North Asian demand, jet was sold slighty lower by a Singapore refiner to a Dutch trader at $30.55 lifting Dec 9-13 fob. Traders said the strong naphtha market again put the squeeze on its spread with gasoline. The spread has dipped as low as $1.95-a-barrel from $2-$3, as gasoline lagged behind naphtha's rise in line with strong crudes. But crude hike has prompted buyers, who were previously sidelined in anticipation of weaker crude, to emerge for December. Singapore refiners were heard with December cargoes but have yet to emerge with offers. Gasoline was dull with a bid for 92-octane heard at $24.85 fob lifting Nov 29-Dec 3. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3084)
